title: Deploy Monte Carlo Risk Simulation Ledger Reconciler
scenario: A finance-ops quantitative cluster runs distributed Monte Carlo pricing simulations and outputs binary checkpoint spools containing trade drift surfaces and variance bounds. The staging deployment orchestrator at `/opt/quant-reconcile/deploy.sh` repeatedly crashes during pre-flight reconciliation, citing fatal SQLite database corruption and worker segmentation faults. The environment contains the orchestration bash scripts, configuration templates, a compiled binary accumulator (`stat_accumulator`), and sample simulation batches in `/opt/quant-reconcile/staging/`.
instruction_draft:
Our overnight quantitative batch runs for portfolio risk simulations are failing to reconcile into the central SQLite database, blocking the morning risk sign-off. The deployment runner at `/opt/quant-reconcile/deploy.sh` aborts during staging verification with fatal SQLite corruption and worker crash errors, leaving `/var/lib/quant-reconcile/reconcile.db` unusable and the systemd-style runner `/usr/local/bin/quant-reconcile-service` undeployed.

Resolve the underlying pipeline and deployment defects so that running `/opt/quant-reconcile/deploy.sh` completes cleanly with exit code 0 and deploys the service. The service configuration in `/etc/quant-reconcile/reconcile.env` and the ingestion pipeline must correctly process worker spool batches into `/var/lib/quant-reconcile/reconcile.db`: every batch must be recorded in `batch_reconcile`, anomalous trades exceeding the configured tolerances must be flagged and logged in `anomaly_records`, worker node tallies must populate `worker_audit`, and the database must pass SQLite integrity checks without WAL shared-memory corruption.
requirements: Running `/opt/quant-reconcile/deploy.sh` must execute to completion with exit code 0.
The deployment must install and configure the service executable at `/usr/local/bin/quant-reconcile-service` with execute permissions.
The configuration file at `/etc/quant-reconcile/reconcile.env` must configure SQLite concurrency safely (`PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`, `PRAGMA busy_timeout >= 5000`, `PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL`).
`/var/lib/quant-reconcile/reconcile.db` must exist and pass `PRAGMA integrity_check;` returning `ok`.
The ingestion pipeline must correctly slice binary scientific records without corrupting float streams or triggering SIGSEGV in `stat_accumulator`.
Error traps in the ingestion scripts must not wipe active POSIX shared-memory files (`/dev/shm/*`) or issue unconditional `SIGKILL` against SQLite processes.
The `batch_reconcile` table must store all processed batch records with correct calculated `mean_drift`, `var_surface`, and status ('MATCHED' or 'DISCREPANCY').
Individual simulation trades exceeding `MAX_DRIFT` or `VAR_LIMIT` defined in `reconcile.env` must be detected using accurate floating-point evaluation and inserted into `anomaly_records`.
The `worker_audit` table must record each worker node's total processed batches, record counts, and input spool checksums.
When `/usr/local/bin/quant-reconcile-service --batch-dir <DIR>` is invoked on fresh, unseen batch spools, it must process all spools cleanly without error and record accurate reconciliation results.
environment: Base image: python:3.13-slim-bookworm with sqlite3, bsdmainutils, gawk, bc, and procps installed.

A compiled x86_64 C binary `/opt/quant-reconcile/bin/stat_accumulator` that reads 64-byte aligned IEEE 754 double precision structs via AVX instructions; segfaults if passed unaligned or truncated text-mangled streams.

Shell script `/opt/quant-reconcile/bin/ingest_batch.sh` (~220 lines) containing: (1) `sed -n '/^---END-HEADER---$/,$p'` that mangles binary records containing 0x0A bytes; (2) a destructive `ERR` trap `pkill -9 -f sqlite3; rm -f /dev/shm/*quant*` that destroys active SQLite WAL `-shm` mapping; (3) integer truncation `printf '%.0f'` on floating-point drift/variance metrics for anomaly detection.
Shell script `/opt/quant-reconcile/bin/reconcile_all.sh` (~90 lines) that dispatches parallel worker ingest jobs with inadequate lock timeout.
Deployment script `/opt/quant-reconcile/deploy.sh` (~110 lines) with flawed pre-flight checks, schema bootstrap (`schema.sql`), and service installation logic.
Staging spools in `/opt/quant-reconcile/staging/` to reproduce the pre-flight crash.
internal_hint: Main difficulty: Not visible by reading (interacting systems and runtime data corruption). When `deploy.sh` runs, the visible error is `SQLITE_CORRUPT: database disk image is malformed` and `stat_accumulator returned exit code 139 (SIGSEGV)`. Agents will intuitively assume either SQLite file corruption or a memory bug in the compiled binary. The actual chain of defects is: 1) `ingest_batch.sh` strips the ASCII metadata header from the spool file using line-oriented `sed` instead of byte-offset extraction (`tail -c +$((HEADER_BYTES + 1))`), which strips or alters newline bytes (0x0A) within the binary IEEE 754 float records, misaligning AVX instructions in `stat_accumulator` and causing SIGSEGV; 2) when `stat_accumulator` crashes, bash's `ERR` trap executes `rm -f /dev/shm/*quant*` and `pkill -9 -f sqlite3`, unlinking active POSIX shared-memory segments while other concurrent worker subshells are mid-transaction, causing SQLite B-tree corruption at offset 4096; 3) in `reconcile.env`, `journal_mode=MEMORY` and `busy_timeout=0` prevent multi-process concurrency, which must be shifted to `WAL` mode with a positive busy timeout; 4) anomaly drift detection in bash uses `printf '%.0f'` instead of `bc -l` or `awk`, rounding fractional drift values to 0.
trap: A solver might attempt to 'fix' SQLite by repeatedly wiping `/var/lib/quant-reconcile/reconcile.db` or patching `schema.sql`, or might conclude `stat_accumulator` is broken and attempt to replace it or bypass it. If they only fix the header slicing on the sample batch, the bash floating-point truncation trap will silently pass the visible samples but fail the hidden seed verification tests where drift values are subtle fractional amounts (e.g. 0.041 vs threshold 0.035).
tests: Verify `/opt/quant-reconcile/deploy.sh` runs cleanly with exit code 0.
Verify `/usr/local/bin/quant-reconcile-service` exists, is executable, and `/etc/quant-reconcile/reconcile.env` sets WAL mode and busy_timeout >= 5000.

Hidden seed instance test: Generate 6 fresh simulation spools using a hidden pseudo-random seed into a temporary directory (containing 4 normal batches and 2 batches with controlled variance and drift anomalies across 3 simulated compute nodes).
Query `batch_reconcile` in `reconcile.db` and assert row count, batch statuses ('MATCHED' vs 'DISCREPANCY'), and numerical aggregates match the reference values within 1e-4 tolerance.
Query `anomaly_records` in `reconcile.db` and assert exactly the expected trade IDs and flag reasons are logged.
Query `worker_audit` and verify record counts and file checksums match reference values for each worker node.
Verify `/dev/shm` contains no orphan unlinked file descriptors or locked SQLite shm files.

verifier_knob.name: number_of_independent_state_properties_checked
verifier_knob.effect: Increasing the knob adds additional stress-testing on concurrent worker batch collisions and edge-case float precision boundaries; decreasing checks only basic deployment exit status and table row counts.

expected_failure_modes: Agent gets misled by the SQLite malformed error and focuses on SQLite recovery commands (.recover, VACUUM) rather than fixing the destructive ERR trap.

Agent suspects `stat_accumulator` has a C memory leak or buffer overflow and wastes time reverse-engineering the binary with objdump/gdb without realizing the input binary stream was corrupted by line-oriented text parsing.
Agent uses integer comparisons in bash for drift thresholds, causing subtle float anomalies generated by the hidden seed to be classified as 'MATCHED' instead of 'DISCREPANCY'.
Agent fixes the staging batch manually or hardcodes answers, failing the verify-time fresh batch spools generated from the hidden seed.
